subject: Renewal: commit sizing, uplift cap, and per-token tiering
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@aperture.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: commit sizing, uplift cap, and per-token tiering

Samir —

Heading into your August renewal, wanted to start a quick thread to align on a right-sized commit and the uplift guardrails you asked about. From our side the key levers are: per-token tiered discounts (hosted API), commit term, and an annual uplift cap we can guarantee on renewal.

A few facts up-front from our telemetry: last 12-week trailing usage averages ~350M tokens/month with two peak weeks around 620M. We included a CSV of the month-by-month token usage for your finance team (attached).

Questions for you:
- Do you expect the forecasted growth to exceed 25% ARR over the next 12 months? If yes, we should plan a larger first-year commit.
- Is a hard annual uplift cap important for procurement (e.g., max +10–15%)?
- Any constraints on term length (12 vs 24 months) or payment cadence?

If you’re free this week Marissa and I can put together 2–3 concrete commit + per-token tier options (including uplift cap) and a DocuSign-ready term sheet.

Thanks —
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Aperture_usage_Jul2026.csv (CSV, 42KB)
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@aperture.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aperture Finance <finance@aperture.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 14:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: commit sizing, uplift cap, and per-token tiering

Thanks Hannah — appreciate the proactive approach.

Quick answers:
- We do expect higher growth from the product team; modeled ~40% YOY but that’s optimistic.
- Procurement cares about predictability; a hard uplift ceiling would be helpful — they quoted 10% as reasonable but we could stretch to 15% with justification.
- Prefer 12-months with quarterly true-ups rather than a 24-month lock.

Attached is a short usage export from our side and a brief note from finance outlining their approval process (they’ll need an explicit uplift cap in the agreement).

Also — can you confirm whether the per-token discounts apply uniformly across prompt+completion tokens or whether embeddings/other endpoints are priced separately in the commit tiers?

Best,
Samir Patel
Head of Platform, Aperture Analytics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@aperture.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 10:30:45 -0700
Subject: Proposed options — commit tiers and uplift cap (Aperture)

Samir / Hannah —

Thanks for the context. Per Hannah’s offer, below are three pragmatic options we can put into the renewal term sheet. I focused on simplicity for procurement and measurable cost outcomes for your engineering spend. I also noted which endpoints are included in the commit buckets.

Option A — Conservative (12 months)- Commit: 3.5B tokens/year (~292M/month)- Per-token discounts: 0–500M: $0.0006; 500M–1.5B: $0.0005; >1.5B: $0.00045- Uplift cap: 10% on annual committed tokens- Endpoints: prompt+completion included; embeddings billed separately at standard embedding SKU- True-up: quarterly (net true-up or invoice)

Option B — Growth (12 months) [recommended]- Commit: 4.5B tokens/year (~375M/month)- Per-token discounts: 0–750M: $0.00055; 750M–1.75B: $0.00047; >1.75B: $0.00042- Uplift cap: 15% on annual committed tokens- Endpoints: prompt+completion included; embeddings included up to 200M tokens, overage at embedding SKU- True-up: quarterly- One-time onboarding credit: 10% of first-quarter usage (applied as invoice credit)

Option C — Aggressive (12 months)- Commit: 6.0B tokens/year (~500M/month)- Per-token discounts: 0–1B: $0.00052; 1B–2.5B: $0.00044; >2.5B: $0.00039- Uplift cap: 20% (requires executive approval)- Embeddings included to higher threshold- True-up: monthly (recommended for large volume)

Notes and constraints:
- Embeddings are a separate compute profile; we can include an embeddings allowance in the commit for Options B/C but need to lock an explicit token bucket.
- The uplift cap is a contractual ceiling on the percent increase of the annual committed token amount at renewal; we can guarantee 15% without exec sign-off.
- We can include a one-time 10% credit on the first quarter (Option B) to offset migration costs.

Next steps:
1) Confirm which option you want to present to procurement.
2) We’ll generate a redlineable term sheet and DocuSign packet (includes the uplift cap clause).
3) If you want tighter uplift cap (<=10%) we’ll route for a small additional discount (typically ~2–3% on per-token).

I attached a draft pricing workbook if you want to run numbers.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0110

Samir —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for sharing Aperture’s preferred constraints. Based on finance and procurement feedback, I’m confirming we can lock Option B (Growth) with the following firm items in the term sheet:
- 4.5B token annual commit (12-month term)
- Per-token tiering as outlined in Option B
- Uplift cap guaranteed at 15% for the next renewal cycle
- Embeddings: 200M tokens included, overage at embedding SKU
- Quarterly true-ups; first-quarter 10% onboarding credit applied as agreed

I’ve attached the DocuSign-ready term sheet. If that looks good to you, sign via the link below and we’ll issue a countersigned copy within 48 hours.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/prepare/abcdef123456
HubSpot: https://app.redwood.in/hubspot/contacts/record/HS-4321

If procurement needs a 10% uplift cap hard-coded instead of 15%, we can offer a 2% additional per-token discount on the same tiers — let me know and I’ll update the packet.

Appreciate the collaboration — looking forward to closing this week.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
